questions.q_en: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the road network in India?
options_en: India has the largest road network in the world.
Roads in India are primarily concentrated in rural and remote areas.
National Highways constitute about 2 percent of the total road length but carry 40 percent of the road traffic.
The Border Roads Organisation was established after the National Highways Authority of India.
questions.solution_en:
National Highways in India form only about 2% of the total road length but carry about 40% of the total road traffic, making them a crucial part of the transportation network.

In contrast:

• India has the second-largest road network after the USA.

• Road development is more intensive in urban and semi-urban areas, not primarily in rural and remote zones.

• The Border Roads Organisation (BRO) was established in 1960, well before the formation of NHAI in 1995.

questions.q_en: The Grand Trunk (GT) road, historically connecting Calcutta and Peshawar, is currently bifurcated into which National Highways?
questions.solution_en:
The historical Grand Trunk Road is primarily split into NH-1 (connecting Delhi to Amritsar) and NH-2 (Delhi to Kolkata), maintaining the historic route between Peshawar and Calcutta (Kolkata).

In contrast:

• NH-8 connects Delhi and Mumbai.

• NH-44 runs from Srinagar to Kanyakumari.

• NH-7 was renumbered and merged into NH-44.

questions.q_en: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) was operationalised in which year?
questions.solution_en:
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) was made operational in 1995 under the NHAI Act of 1988. It is responsible for the development, maintenance, and management of National Highways.

In contrast:

• 1943 and 1951 predate the idea of a centralized highways authority.

• 2020 is incorrect as NHAI was well established by then.

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding rail transport in India:

A. Indian Railways was introduced in 1853, with the first line from Bombay to Thane.

B. Indian Railways network is divided into 12 zones.

C. The broad gauge has a distance of 1.676 metres between the rails.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution_en:
Statements A and C are correct:

• The first Indian railway line was inaugurated on April 16, 1853, between Bombay and Thane.

• The Indian broad gauge track width is 1.676 meters.

• However, the Indian Railways network is divided into 18 zones, not 12.
questions.solution_hi:
Statements A and C are correct:

• The first Indian railway line was inaugurated on April 16, 1853, between Bombay and Thane.

• The Indian broad gauge track width is 1.676 meters.

• However, the Indian Railways network is divided into 18 zones, not 12.

questions.q_en: The Konkan Railway, connecting Roha in Maharashtra to Mangalore in Karnataka, is notable for:
options_en: Being the longest railway route in India
Having the highest average altitude of any Indian railway
questions.solution_en:
The Konkan Railway is known for its engineering marvels, including crossing over 146 rivers and using nearly 2000 bridges along the route through a rugged terrain.

In contrast:

• It's not the longest railway route.

• It doesn't operate at the highest altitude (that title belongs to routes in the Himalayas).

• It uses broad gauge, not metre gauge.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is the most fuel-efficient and eco-friendly mode of transport in India, suitable for carrying heavy and bulky materials?
questions.solution_en:
Waterways are the most fuel-efficient and eco-friendly mode of transport. They consume less fuel per tonne-kilometer and are ideal for carrying bulky and heavy goods.

In contrast:

• Roadways are less efficient due to traffic and fuel consumption.

• Railways are better than roadways but still less efficient than waterways.

• Airways are the least fuel-efficient and suited only for high-value, low-weight cargo.

questions.q_en:

b. NW 2 (Sadiya - Dhubri) - ii. West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh

c. NW 3 (Kottapuram - Kollam) - iii. Assam
questions.solution_en:

In contrast:

• Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Goa also have coastal regions but do not possess such extensive backwater systems.

• Air and land routes handle far less trade volume, mainly high-value or neighboring country trade.

questions.q_en:
Assertion (A): Waterways are the cheapest means of transport in India, especially for heavy and bulky materials.

Reason (R): Diversion of river water for irrigation purposes has made some rivers non-navigable in large parts of their courses.
options_en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.solution_en:
Waterways are indeed the cheapest mode of transport for heavy and bulky goods due to low fuel consumption and maintenance costs.

While it's also true that irrigation diversion has made some rivers non-navigable, this is not the reason waterways are cheap.

Therefore:

• Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A directly.

questions.q_en: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the development of railways in India during the British colonial era?
options_en: Areas around towns were well-connected by railways.
Raw material producing areas were connected by railways for exploitation of resources.
Hill stations and cantonment towns were connected by railways.
Railway routes were primarily developed to connect rural agricultural areas with each other.
questions.solution_en:
Railways during the colonial period were mainly laid out to serve British economic and administrative interests - connecting ports, resource-rich areas, and strategic military points like cantonments and hill stations.

In contrast:

• Rural agricultural areas were often neglected unless they produced exportable resources.

questions.q_en: The Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) gas pipeline, a major artery in India's gas market development, was constructed by:
questions.solution_en:
GAIL constructed the HVJ pipeline, India's first cross-country natural gas pipeline, which became crucial in developing India's gas-based economy.

In contrast:

• Other corporations primarily focus on refining or distribution.

Further information:

The first cross-country pipeline in Asia connected the oil fields at Naharkatiya in Assam to Barauni in Bihar, enabling crude oil transport.

The National Highways constitute only about 2 per cent of the total road length but carry 40 per cent of the road traffic.
